thread:
jen (sales): Quick preflight for GraniteHealth POC next week — need confirmations on SSO/SCIM/RBAC + a rough number for dedicated POC pricing. Alex, which domains should we lock to?

alex (GraniteHealth): Primary is granitehealth.com. Also prod.granitehealth.com and staging.granitehealth.net for test traffic. We want strict domain controls for production only.

mike (solutions): Got it. For domain locking we can do both claim-based and DNS TXT verification. Recommend DNS TXT for authoritative ownership for prod. Quick SAML checklist: 
- ACS (consume URL): https://api.redwood.ai/saml/acs/gh-poc
- EntityID: https://redwood.ai/metadata/gh-poc
- NameID: persistent (email or transient if you prefer)
- Support encrypted assertions: yes (we can accept AES-256)
- SP-initiated + IdP-initiated: both supported

If you want, I can send a metadata XML to your IdP admin.

jen (sales): Alex — do you need group claims in the SAML assertion or would you prefer SCIM group sync be the source of truth for RBAC mapping?

alex (GraniteHealth): SCIM source-of-truth preferred. We have Okta pushing group membership; would rather one-way sync.

mike (solutions): Perfect — we'll map SCIM groups -> Redwood roles. For clarity, RECOMMENDED mapping: 
- scim group "engineers" -> role "developer"
- scim group "ops" -> role "platform-admin"
- scim group "guest-contractors" -> role "restricted"

SCIM endpoints for the POC: 
- Base: https://api.redwood.ai/scim/gh-poc/v2
- Bearer token: we'll generate per-environment (no shared creds)

Example SCIM create payload we tested with Okta (paste into Okta provisioning):

```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "j.smith@granitehealth.com",
  "name": {"givenName": "John","familyName": "Smith"},
  "emails": [{"value": "j.smith@granitehealth.com","primary": true}],
  "active": true,
  "externalId": "okta-12345",
  "groups": [{"value": "engineers"}]
}
```

mike (solutions): Note: include `externalId` to help reconcile duplicate accounts. Also recommend we run a small delta sync cadence (5–15m) during POC.

devon (security): A few security checklist items from our side: 
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys? (yes/no)
- Audit log retention window needed (we can extend for POC)
- Do you require IP allowlist / VPC peering for the POC?
- Any specific encryption in transit extras (mTLS)?

alex (GraniteHealth): We'll need KMS for logs at rest and 365d retention for audit logs. VPC peering preferred for prod but for POC we can start with IP allowlist. No mTLS initially.

devon (security): Cool. We can enable KMS and 365d retention on the POC tenancy. For VPC peering on Dedicated we need networking info — i'll send a template. Also, we'll provide SOC2 + data processing addendum (DPA) docs.

tara (legal): Re: security questionnaire — can you send us the standard vendor sec-qa? We have a couple custom redact requests but should be fine. Jenkins/Okta integration needs answers on user provisioning scope.

jen (sales): On pricing: quick options for the POC window (2 weeks): 
1) Hosted POC: shared capacity, limited SLA — free credits available, lower cost but no dedicated throughput guarantees.
2) Dedicated POC: reserved 1x GPU pool for two weeks — flat fee estimate $6k–$10k depending on instance size and priority. Includes VPC peering option.
3) Private (on-prem/VPC): if you need private control plane, that would be multi-week setup and enterprise contract.

jen (sales): Alex — which route do you want to prioritize? If dedicated, we need signed order form + network CIDR for peering by EOD Friday to hit the timeline.

alex (GraniteHealth): Let's do Dedicated POC. I'll get the network CIDR and PO to you tomorrow. Is there an ops checklist for the peering change?

mike (solutions): Yes — I'll drop the peering checklist and the DNS TXT template for domain verification in this thread as a one-pager. Short version: 
- Provide VPC CIDR + contact email
- Set up route table entries after peer accept
- Add DNS TXT record: "redwood-verification=gh-poc-<token>" for each domain to verify ownership

jen (sales): One more thing — for RBAC smoke tests during POC can we get 3 test users from each group (engineers, ops, contractors)? We can stage a canary policy rollout to validate restrictions.

alex (GraniteHealth): Yes, will provision test accounts.

mike (solutions): Great. I'll queue a canary rollout and set up tracing hooks so we can show token-level latency during demo. Anything else?

devon (security): Please attach the completed vendor sec-qa to the PO as well. We'll fast-track the answers.

jen (sales): Thanks everyone — I'll follow up w/ metadata XML, SCIM token, and the dedicated POC invoice draft. /cc @mike @devon

alex (GraniteHealth): Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
